learn.b: Say Hallo for hello. Use Guten Morgen in the morning, Guten Tag during the day, Guten Abend in the evening and Gute Nacht before bed. To say goodbye, use Tschüss or Auf Wiedersehen.
Say Ich heiße and your name: Ich heiße Anna means My name is Anna. Ask Wie geht's? to say How are you? and answer Gut, danke.
Danke means thank you and Bitte means please or you're welcome. All German nouns start with a capital letter.

qs.q: How do you say 'good morning' in German?
qs.why: Guten Morgen is used to greet people in the morning.

qs.q: What does 'Ich heiße Anna' mean?
Which word means 'thank you'?
qs.why: Danke is the German word for thank you.

qs.q: What does 'Wie geht's?' ask?
'Tschüss' means 'goodbye'.

learn.b: Count like this: eins, zwei, drei, vier, fünf, sechs, sieben, acht, neun, zehn. Use them for ages, prices and phone numbers.
Rot is red, blau is blue, grün is green and gelb is yellow. Learn them together with the nouns, like der Apfel (the apple).
Learn das Brot (bread), das Wasser (water), der Apfel (apple) and die Milch (milk). To ask politely, say Ich möchte. Ich möchte Wasser means I would like water.

qs.q: What is 'sieben' in English?
Which word means 'green'?

'Die Milch' means 'milk'.

learn.b: Learn die Mutter (mother), der Vater (father), der Bruder (brother) and die Schwester (sister). Der, die and das all mean 'the'.
Sein has the forms ich bin (I am), du bist (you are) and er ist (he is). Ich bin Schüler means I am a pupil.
Haben has the forms ich habe (I have), du hast (you have) and er hat (he has). Ich habe einen Bruder means I have a brother.

qs.q: What does 'die Schwester' mean?
Complete: Ich ___ Schüler. (I am a pupil)
qs.why: Bin is the 'I' form of sein (to be).

qs.q: How do you say 'I have a brother'?
qs.why: Habe is the 'I' form of haben (to have).

qs.q: Complete: Sie ___ zwei Katzen. (She has two cats)
qs.why: Hat is the 'he or she' form of haben.

learn.b: German has three words for 'the': der, die and das. The plural is always die. Plurals change in different ways: das Buch becomes die Bücher.
The days are Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag, Freitag, Samstag and Sonntag. They are written with a capital letter.
Use Wo ist...? to ask where something is. Wo ist die Schule? means Where is the school? Das Haus (house) uses das.

qs.q: Which article goes with 'Haus' (house)?
qs.why: Haus is neuter, so it uses das.

qs.q: What is the plural of 'Buch' (book)?
qs.why: The plural of das Buch is die Bücher.

qs.q: What does 'Mittwoch' mean?
What does 'Wo ist die Schule?' ask?
'Samstag' means Sunday.
qs.why: Samstag is Saturday; Sunday is Sonntag.

lab.hint: The plural article is die and the vowel changes.

learn.b: Regular verbs drop -en and add endings. Wohnen (to live): ich wohne, du wohnst, er/sie wohnt, wir wohnen, ihr wohnt, sie wohnen. Lernen (to learn) works the same way.
Ask Woher kommst du? (Where do you come from?). Answer Ich komme aus Italien (I come from Italy). Say Ich wohne in Berlin for where you live.
In a German statement the verb is always the second idea. Ich lerne Deutsch. Heute lerne ich Deutsch. The verb stays second even when a time word comes first.

qs.q: Complete: Ich ___ in Berlin.
qs.why: With ich the verb ends in -e.

What does 'Woher kommst du?' mean?
Complete: Er ___ Fußball. (spielen)
In 'Heute spiele ich Tennis' the verb is in second place.
qs.why: The verb stays second even after a time word.

learn.b: Elf is 11 and zwölf is 12. Then add -zehn: dreizehn (13), vierzehn (14), fünfzehn (15). Zwanzig is 20.
The tens are zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig and hundert is 100. German says the one first: einundzwanzig means one-and-twenty (21). Age: Ich bin zwanzig Jahre alt.
Ask Wie spät ist es? Answer Es ist drei Uhr (It is three o'clock). Uhr means o'clock or clock. Months are Januar, Februar, März, April and so on.

learn.b: Das Haus is the house and die Wohnung is the apartment. Rooms: die Küche (kitchen), das Bad (bathroom), das Schlafzimmer (bedroom), das Wohnzimmer (living room).
Die Stadt is the city and die Straße is the street. Learn der Park (park) and der Supermarkt (supermarket). Der Supermarkt is where you buy food.
Say Ich wohne in einer Wohnung (I live in an apartment) or Ich wohne in einem Haus. Describe a room with ist: Das Zimmer ist groß (The room is big).

What is 'das Schlafzimmer'?

qs.why: Die Stadt is the city or town.

learn.b: Wer is who, was is what, wo is where, wann is when, warum is why and wie is how. Wo wohnst du? means Where do you live? The question word comes first and the verb second.
For a yes or no question the verb goes first: Hast du einen Bruder? (Do you have a brother?). Answer Ja or Nein.
Use kein for nouns with ein or no article: Ich habe kein Auto, Ich habe keinen Bruder. Use nicht for verbs and adjectives: Ich bin nicht müde (I am not tired).

qs.q: What does 'was' mean?
What does 'Wo wohnst du?' mean?

qs.why: Kein negates a noun: kein Auto.

qs.q: Complete: Ich bin ___ müde.

qs.why: Yes or no questions start with the verb.

learn.b: Die Hose is the trousers, das T-Shirt is the T-shirt, der Pullover is the sweater and die Jacke is the jacket. Die Schuhe means the shoes and is always plural.
Ask Wie viel kostet das? (How much does that cost?). Answer Das kostet zehn Euro. Use the numbers you know for the price.
Es regnet means it is raining and es schneit means it is snowing. Die Sonne scheint means the sun is shining. Es ist kalt, warm or heiß describes the temperature.

What does 'Es regnet' mean?

learn.b: Ich spiele Gitarre (I play guitar), ich höre Musik (I listen to music), ich lese Bücher (I read books). Add gern to say you like doing it: Ich schwimme gern.
Können means can: ich kann, du kannst. Möchten means would like: ich möchte. Müssen means must: ich muss.
A modal verb is second and the other verb goes to the end in the infinitive. Ich kann gut schwimmen means I can swim well. Ich muss lernen means I have to study.

qs.q: What does 'Ich schwimme gern' mean?
qs.why: Gern means gladly, so it shows you like it.

qs.q: What does 'Ich kann Gitarre spielen' mean?

qs.why: Ich kann is the correct form.

qs.why: After a modal verb the infinitive goes to the end.

learn.b: Most verbs use haben plus a past participle at the end. Ich habe Pizza gegessen means I ate pizza. Wir haben gespielt means we played.
Verbs of movement and change, like gehen (to go) and fahren (to drive), use sein. Ich bin ins Kino gegangen means I went to the cinema.
Use gestern (yesterday), heute Morgen (this morning), letzte Woche (last week) and letztes Jahr (last year). They show the action is finished.

qs.q: Complete: Gestern ___ ich Pizza gegessen. (I ate)
qs.why: Essen uses haben: ich habe gegessen.

qs.q: What does 'Wir haben gespielt' mean?
qs.why: Wir haben gespielt is the Perfekt: we played.

qs.q: Which helper verb does 'gehen' use in the Perfekt?
qs.why: Gehen is a verb of movement and takes sein.

qs.q: What does 'gestern' mean?

qs.why: Ich bin gegangen is the Perfekt of gehen: I went.

learn.b: Use links (left), rechts (right) and geradeaus (straight ahead). An der Ecke means at the corner.
In der Nähe von means near and weit weg means far away. To ask the way, say Wie komme ich zum Bahnhof? (How do I get to the station?).
Learn der Bahnhof (station), der Flughafen (airport), die Fahrkarte (ticket) and das Zimmer (room). Use buchen for to book.

qs.why: Links means left; rechts means right.

learn.b: Use ich mag (I like) and ich finde...gut (I think...is good). Ich mag Musik means I like music. Say ich mag nicht or ich finde...schlecht for the negative.
Say ich denke, dass... for I think that... The verb goes to the end after dass: Ich denke, dass es gut ist. Say ich bin einverstanden for I agree.
Use lieber to say you prefer something: Ich spiele lieber Fußball. Weil means because and besser als means better than. The verb also goes to the end after weil.

qs.why: After dass, the verb goes to the end of the clause.

learn.b: Use werden plus a verb for the future: Ich werde reisen means I will travel. You can also use the present with a time word: Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin.
Many routine verbs split in two: ich stehe um sieben auf (I get up at seven). Others are reflexive: ich ziehe mich an (I get dressed). Ich gehe ins Bett means I go to bed.
In the simple past, ich bin becomes ich war (I was). It is often used instead of the Perfekt. Time words include nächstes Jahr (next year) and immer (always).

qs.q: Complete: Morgen ___ ich nach Berlin reisen. (I will travel)
qs.why: Werden + a verb at the end forms the future.

o: I go to bed at seven

qs.q: What does 'ich war' mean?
qs.why: War is the simple past of sein.

qs.q: What does 'nächstes Jahr' mean?

learn.b: Dürfen means to be allowed to: ich darf, du darfst. Sollen means should: ich soll, du sollst. Wollen means to want to: ich will, du willst. Müssen means must: ich muss.
The modal verb is second and the main verb goes to the end: Ich darf hier parken. Du sollst mehr Wasser trinken. Wir wollen nach Spanien fahren.
Ich darf nicht means I am not allowed to. Ich muss nicht means I do not have to. They are different, so be careful.

qs.q: What does 'Ich darf hier nicht rauchen' mean?

I am not allowed to smoke here
I do not have to smoke here

qs.q: Complete: Du ___ mehr Wasser trinken. (should)
What does 'Ich muss nicht arbeiten' mean?

I do not want to work
I do not have to work
qs.why: Muss nicht means no need to.

qs.q: What does 'wollen' mean?
In 'Ich will nach Spanien fahren' the verb fahren goes to the end.
qs.why: The main verb goes to the end with a modal.

learn.b: In the dative, der and das become dem, die becomes der, and plural die becomes den (and the noun adds -n). Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch (I give the man the book).
Mit, nach, bei, zu, von, aus and seit always take the dative. Ich fahre mit dem Bus. Ich wohne bei meiner Tante (with my aunt). Zu der becomes zur and zu dem becomes zum.
Say Ich gehe zur Schule or Er kommt aus der Schweiz. After each of these prepositions look for the dative form.

qs.q: Complete: Ich fahre mit ___ Bus.
qs.why: Mit takes the dative; der Bus becomes dem Bus.

What does 'Ich wohne bei meiner Tante' mean?

learn.b: Der Kopf is the head, der Bauch the stomach, der Arm the arm, das Bein the leg, die Hand the hand, der Fuß the foot, das Auge the eye.
Say Ich habe Kopfschmerzen (I have a headache) or Ich habe Bauchschmerzen (stomachache). Say Ich bin krank for I am sick. Mir geht es nicht gut means I do not feel well.
Der Arzt or die Ärztin is the doctor. Say Ich brauche einen Termin (I need an appointment). Buy medicine in die Apotheke (the pharmacy).

learn.b: Der Lehrer is the teacher, der Koch the cook, der Arzt the doctor, der Ingenieur the engineer. Women add -in: die Lehrerin. Ask Was bist du von Beruf? (What is your job?).
Say Ich bin Lehrer with no article. Or Ich arbeite als Koch (I work as a cook). Der Beruf is the profession.
Die Schule is school, die Universität is university and das Fach is the school subject. Studieren means to study at university: Ich studiere Medizin. Lernen is to learn.

What does 'Ich arbeite als Koch' mean?

learn.b: Add -er to make the comparative: groß becomes größer, schnell becomes schneller, klein becomes kleiner. Use als for than: Er ist größer als ich.
Use am plus -sten: am schnellsten (fastest). Gut is irregular: gut, besser, am besten. Viel is viel, mehr, am meisten. Gern is gern, lieber, am liebsten.
Use so ... wie for equal things: Er ist so groß wie ich (He is as tall as me). Use nicht so ... wie for less: Sie ist nicht so alt wie er.

learn.b: Weil (because), dass (that), wenn (if, when) and obwohl (although) send the verb to the end. Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin. Ich gehe spazieren, obwohl es kalt ist.
Start with wenn: Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause. After the comma the verb comes first in the main clause.
Use würde plus an infinitive: Ich würde gern reisen (I would like to travel). Use hätte and wäre for would have and would be: Wenn ich reich wäre, würde ich ein Haus kaufen.

learn.b: Say Ciao for a casual hi or bye. Use Buongiorno in the morning, Buonasera in the evening and Buonanotte before bed. To say goodbye politely, use Arrivederci.
Say Mi chiamo and your name: Mi chiamo Marco means My name is Marco. Ask Come stai? to say How are you? and answer Sto bene (I am well).
Grazie means thank you and Prego means you're welcome. Per favore means please.

learn.b: Count like this: uno, due, tre, quattro, cinque, sei, sette, otto, nove, dieci. Use them for ages, prices and phone numbers.
Rosso is red, blu is blue, verde is green and giallo is yellow. Colors usually come after the noun: la mela rossa means the red apple.
Learn il pane (bread), l'acqua (water), la mela (apple) and il latte (milk). To ask politely, say Vorrei. Vorrei acqua means I would like water.

learn.b: Learn la madre (mother), il padre (father), il fratello (brother) and la sorella (sister). Il goes with most masculine words and la with feminine words.
Essere has the forms io sono (I am), tu sei (you are) and lui è (he is). Io sono studente means I am a student.
Avere has the forms io ho (I have), tu hai (you have) and lui ha (he has). Ho un fratello means I have a brother.

learn.b: Use il or la for 'the' with one thing, and i or le for many. Un and una mean 'a'. Plurals change the ending: libro becomes libri and casa becomes case.
The days are lunedì, martedì, mercoledì, giovedì, venerdì, sabato and domenica. They are written with a small first letter.
Use Dov'è...? to ask where something is. Dov'è la scuola? means Where is the school? La casa (house) and la scuola (school) are both feminine.

learn.b: Italian verbs end in -are, -ere or -ire. Parlare (to speak): parlo, parli, parla, parliamo, parlate, parlano. Abitare (to live) works the same way: io abito, tu abiti.
Ask Di dove sei? (Where are you from?). Answer Sono di Milano. Say Abito a Roma for where you live.
Italian often drops io, tu and lui because the ending shows the person. Parlo italiano means I speak Italian. Leggo is I read and dormo is I sleep.

learn.b: Undici is 11 and dodici is 12. Then tredici (13), quattordici (14), quindici (15). Venti is 20.
The tens are venti, trenta, quaranta, cinquanta. Cento is 100. Ventuno is 21. Say your age with Ho venti anni (I have twenty years).
Ask Che ore sono? (What time is it?). Answer Sono le tre (It is three o'clock). For one o'clock say È l'una. Months are gennaio, febbraio, marzo and so on, with a small letter.

learn.b: La casa is the house and l'appartamento is the apartment. Rooms: la cucina (kitchen), il bagno (bathroom), la camera da letto (bedroom), il soggiorno (living room).
La città is the city, la strada is the street and la piazza is the square. Learn il parco (park) and il supermercato (supermarket).
Say Abito in un appartamento (I live in an apartment) or Abito in una casa. Describe a room with è: La camera è grande (The room is big).

learn.b: Chi is who, che cosa or cosa is what, dove is where, quando is when, perché is why or because and come is how. Dove abiti? means Where do you live?
Keep the same word order and raise your voice: Hai un fratello? (Do you have a brother?). Answer Sì or No.
Put non before the verb: Non ho fame (I am not hungry), Non sono stanco (I am not tired). Non ho un fratello means I do not have a brother.

Ask Quanto costa? (How much does it cost?). Answer Costa dieci euro. Use the numbers you know for the price.
Piove means it is raining and nevica means it is snowing. Say C'è il sole for it is sunny. Italian uses fa for temperature: fa freddo (it is cold) and fa caldo (it is hot).

learn.b: Suono la chitarra (I play guitar), ascolto la musica (I listen to music), leggo libri (I read books), ballo (I dance). Say Mi piace nuotare for I like swimming.
Potere means can: posso, puoi. Volere means want: voglio, vuoi. Dovere means must: devo, devi. Vorrei means I would like.
The second verb stays in the infinitive: Posso nuotare (I can swim). Devo studiare (I have to study). Voglio ballare (I want to dance).

learn.b: Most verbs use avere plus a past participle. Ho mangiato means I ate. Abbiamo parlato means we spoke. For -are verbs, the participle ends in -ato.
Verbs of movement, like andare (to go) and arrivare (to arrive), use essere. Sono andato al cinema means I went to the cinema. A girl writes andata.
Use ieri (yesterday), ieri sera (last night), la settimana scorsa (last week) and l'anno scorso (last year). They show the action is finished.

Vicino a means near and lontano da means far from. To ask the way, say Come arrivo alla stazione? (How do I get to the station?).
Learn la stazione (station), l'aeroporto (airport), il biglietto (ticket) and la camera (room). Use prenotare for to book.

learn.b: Use mi piace with one thing and mi piacciono with many things. Mi piace il cinema means I like cinema. Mi piacciono i libri means I like books. Say non mi piace for I don't like.
Say penso che or secondo me to mean I think that or in my opinion. Say sono d'accordo for I agree and non sono d'accordo for I disagree.
Preferisco means I prefer. Più...di means more than. After penso che, Italian uses the subjunctive, like sia (is): Penso che sia bello.

learn.b: Use andare a + a verb to talk about plans: vado a viaggiare means I am going to travel. Add words like domani (tomorrow) or l'anno prossimo (next year).
Reflexive verbs use mi: mi alzo (I get up), mi lavo (I wash) and mi sveglio (I wake up). Vado a letto means I go to bed.
The imperfetto talks about habits in the past. Giocavo means I used to play. Use words like sempre (always) and da piccolo (as a child).

Follow the modal with an infinitive: Posso entrare? (May I come in?). Voglio mangiare (I want to eat). Devi studiare (You must study).
Say Mi dispiace, non posso venire (Sorry, I cannot come). Non voglio means I do not want to. Dobbiamo partire means we have to leave.

learn.b: When a, di, in, da or su meet il, la or l', they often join. A + il becomes al, a + la becomes alla, di + il becomes del, in + la becomes nella, da + il becomes dal.
Vado al mercato (I go to the market). Sono nella cucina (I am in the kitchen). Il libro del ragazzo (the boy's book). Vengo dalla Francia (I come from France).
Use da for people and places of work: Vado dal medico (I go to the doctor). Vado dal dentista. Use a for most places: Vado a Roma.

Il medico is the doctor. Say Ho bisogno di un appuntamento (I need an appointment). Buy medicine at la farmacia (the pharmacy).

learn.b: Use più for more and meno for less. Marco è più alto di Luca (Marco is taller than Luca). Use di before a noun or pronoun and che between two adjectives or verbs.
Add the article: il più alto (the tallest). Buono becomes migliore and bene becomes meglio: Sto meglio oggi (I feel better today). Add -issimo for very: bellissimo means very beautiful.
Use (così) ... come for equal things: Sono alto come te (I am as tall as you). Use meno ... di for less than.

learn.b: Use se (if) with the present for real conditions: Se piove, resto a casa (If it rains, I stay home). Anche se means even if or although. Mentre means while.
The conditional says would. Mangiare becomes mangerei (I would eat), andare becomes andrei (I would go), volere becomes vorrei (I would like).
Mi piacerebbe viaggiare means I would like to travel. Vorrei un caffè is a polite order. Use perché for because.
